decision-tree.root-question: Is the codebase edited by an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor or similar) on a recurring basis?

branch.conclusion: Skip this methodology. The rubric pays for itself only where an agent reads the tree every day; a human-only codebase gets a normal architecture review.

branch.question: Was the audit produced by `llm-arch-audit.sh` (or the project's committed equivalent) with the command and commit SHA recorded?

branch.conclusion: Rerun the committed script on the current SHA and cite command plus SHA in `evidence[]` before drawing any conclusion.

branch.question: Does the audit list any barrel files or wildcard imports?

branch.conclusion: Remove barrels and star imports first; they hide symbol locations and invalidate every other finding about file navigation.

branch.question: Does any file exceed the recorded `line_limit`, or any path exceed 3 directory levels?

branch.conclusion: Decision names the specific files to split (data out, hooks out, utils out) and the paths to flatten, ranked by size.
Baseline is clean: commit `CLAUDE.md` with the same line limit and conventions, and wire the audit command into CI.

example.p: Codebase edited daily by Claude Code. Audit run via `bash templates/llm-arch-audit.sh src 250` on SHA `a1b2c3d`; barrel section lists `src/components/index.ts` → r-no-barrel-reexports: delete the barrel and rewrite 14 imports, then rerun to reach the file-size branch.
